rubric.name: literature-reading-reference plan r3 (second round)
criteria: MVP first: classify every concern as blocking, hardening, or completeness, and report blocking concerns first. A concern is blocking only if, left unfixed, a phase cannot be specified, implemented and tested as the plan writes it, or the software would not demonstrably do what the plan claims. Do not manufacture completeness concerns to avoid an empty return -- "no concerns, and here is what I checked" is a valid answer.

This is the second and final review round. The first round reviewed r2; its report is .gnd-planning/reviews/literature-reading-reference-r2-panel/PANEL-REVIEW.md (context only). Section 11 maps its seven fixes to sites in r3. For each fix, say whether r3 resolves it, and report any new inconsistency a fix introduced.
Rows tagged (o) (D6) and the owner rulings quoted in section 8 are owner rulings. Do not re-argue them; report only a ruling applied inconsistently or one that makes a criterion impossible.

For each phase LR1 to LR3, can it be specified, implemented and tested as sections 2 and 4 write it, with the lanes section 9 names, within the scope sections 2 and 7 state? LR3 is deliberately an outline that waits for literature-host-interfaces LH1 and LH2 and for owner rulings; judge whether that dependency and its gate are clear, not whether LR3 is fully specified.

Does each code location, line number, command result and quoted message cited in the plan (notably section 1, H1 to H25) match the repository at this checkout? Cite the plan line and name the source file and line in the observation.
Every concern's evidence must quote the plan file. The draft LR1 spec (notes/phase-LR1-spec.md), the milestone README and the first-round report are context only, not under review.
